title: Decomposers and the Cycle of Matter
seo_title: Grade 5 Decomposers Worksheets: Bacteria, Fungi, Compost and the Cycle of Matter
standard_text: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on decomposers and the cycle of matter (NGSS 5-LS2-1): bacteria, fungi and earthworms, compost data, and how matter moves among plants, animals, soil and air. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Decomposers return matter from dead things to the soil and air.
key_sub: Matter cycles: plants take in air and water, animals eat plants, and bacteria and fungi break down the dead so the matter is used again.
body_html:
How to think about it

Matter moves around an ecosystem in a cycle. It is not used up; it is used again and again.

  • Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air and water (and a few nutrients) from the soil to build their bodies.
  • Animals eat plants or other animals. They breathe out carbon dioxide and leave wastes.
  • Decomposers, mainly bacteria and fungi, break down dead plants, dead animals and wastes. Earthworms and other soil animals help. Nutrients go back to the soil and carbon dioxide goes back to the air.
Example

A leaf falls and rots. Where does its matter go?

Fungi and bacteria break the leaf down.

Nutrients go into the soil; carbon dioxide and water go into the air.

Answer: Back into the soil and air, for plants to use again.

Example

Bread molds in 5 days on a warm, damp counter and in 30 days in the fridge. Why?

Mold is a decomposer.

Decomposers grow faster where it is warm and moist.

Answer: Warmth speeds up decomposers.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dead things just disappear. Decomposers turn them into nutrients and gases.
  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil. They build their bodies mostly from air and water.
  • Thinking matter is used up. It cycles and is reused.
  • Thinking all bacteria and fungi are harmful. Decomposers are needed in every ecosystem.

faq.a: They break down dead plants, dead animals and wastes. This returns nutrients to the soil and carbon dioxide to the air, so plants can use the matter again.
Bacteria and fungi, such as mold and mushrooms. Earthworms, pill bugs and millipedes help by breaking dead matter into small pieces.

faq.q: Why is the cycle of matter important?
faq.a: Matter is not used up. It moves again and again among air, soil, plants, animals and decomposers, so living things always have materials to grow.
Warmth and moisture. Food rots faster on a warm, damp counter than in the fridge.
